title: Login never applies the configured auth rate limit

evidence.quote: async def login(... request: Request ...): ... if not user: ... if not verify_password(...):

reasoning: The /auth/login handler accepts the Request but never calls the imported auth rate limiter before username lookup or password verification. The only check_auth_rate_limit calls in this file are duplicated after a return statement in a different route, so they are unreachable and cannot limit login attempts. This leaves password guessing against /auth/login unbounded by the app-level auth limiter.
recommendation: Move a single check_auth_rate_limit(request) call into the start of login before any credential validation, and remove the unreachable duplicated calls after revoke_api_token's return.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and no inspected backend test exercises repeated failed /auth/login attempts or expects a 429 response from the auth limiter.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI TestClient test that enables auth rate limiting, posts invalid credentials to /auth/login from the same client more than the configured limit, and asserts the next response is 429.
minimumFixScope: app/api/auth.py: add the rate-limit check at the top of login and delete the unreachable trailing calls.
